notes.product: Write the53-bit mantissa as L+2^32*H. The three-product32-bit squares and four-product32x21 cross preserve every carry. Their exact sum L^2+2^33*L*H+2^64*H^2 is the106-bit significand square. Carry from the two16-bit cross terms is explicitly added as2^16 to the high partial word; subsequent ADC chains preserve both doubling and three-word addition carries.
notes.grid: For stored input exponent e, x=S*2^(e-1075), P=S^2. Its leading bit selects n=0/1 and biased output exponent E=2e-1023+n. Normal drop52+n; subnormal drop1076-2e. The source53-E+n reduces to that same subnormal grid. At each word branch, retained bits equal P>>s, guard equals P bit(s-1), and sticky is OR of all lower bits. Register shifts by32 intentionally yield0. RNE increment is exactly guard&&(sticky||retained_odd).
notes.classification: e<485 gives x^2<2^-1076, below half-minsubnormal. e1535..2046 gives x^2>=2^1024. e2047 separately distinguishesInfinity/NaN; NaNs preserve input sign/payload and set quiet. Finite and zero squares return positive sign. e1534 cannot round through the overflow midpoint.
notes.actual_ties: Only normal shift53 actual square ties are possible: significand odd*2^26 above sqrt(2)*2^52. Their retained quotient is necessarily even. Subnormal shifts and normal shift52 cannot be exact square midpoints. Odd-parity ties in arbitrary-product model are synthetic controls, never mislabeled as actual square inputs.
notes.dispatch: Nonzero low32(y) goes directly to the identical old dispatcher before any added action. Lowwordzero checks both signedzero,1,-1,+half,2,-half. Half/inverse-root cold cases restore original y registers and go to the old dispatcher. Ordinary receives only lowwordzero nonzero y with all old prefix exact cases already rejected. Its unchanged common source tail preserves every action. Three aliases refer to existing function addresses and add no storage.
notes.sNaN_zero: For y=+/-0 the wrapper identifies a NaN from exponent/fraction with sign ignored. A quiet NaN returns1, as doesInfinity. Signalling NaN returns original input payload/sign with quiet bit set; no dispatcher frame is allocated. y=1 still quiets any NaN while retaining all other input bits.
